detail.text: Glen on the 20th. Zero snow anywhere near the trail, the north side chute of legend is just blocky talus. Rae Lakes warm enough to swim. Carried spikes 90 miles for nothing, which is the best possible outcome.

ledger.title: Update: I made it and so can you

detail.author: u/firsttimerjmt

extraction.quote_span: snow is patchy at worst on every pass now

detail.quote: snow is patchy at worst on every pass now
detail.text: Follow up to my Glen Pass panic post. Finished at Whitney on the 18th. By the time we hit Muir on the 14th everything felt easy, snow is patchy at worst on every pass now. If a scared first timer like me can do it in this snow year, you can too. Still bring spikes for the early mornings.

detail.author: u/quietfeet_22

extraction.quote_span: the famous snowfield is down to maybe 80 feet with a boot trench you could push a stroller through

detail.quote: the famous snowfield is down to maybe 80 feet with a boot trench you could push a stroller through
detail.text: SOBO the last two days. Pinchot 7/7 basically clear, one snow patch below the top on the north. Glen 7/8, the famous snowfield is down to maybe 80 feet with a boot trench you could push a stroller through. Did not take my spikes off my pack all week. Woods Creek bridge makes life easy, Bubbs knee high.

extraction.quote_span: north side snowfield is going fast, boot path is deep and obvious, spikes for the first hour only

detail.quote: north side snowfield is going fast, boot path is deep and obvious, spikes for the first hour only
detail.text: Glen 6/22: north side snowfield is going fast, boot path is deep and obvious, spikes for the first hour only. Pinchot 6/23: patchy snow, no traction needed anywhere. Woods Creek was the sketchiest crossing so far, waist deep and pushy at 4pm. Cross early.

detail.author: u/firsttimerjmt

extraction.quote_span: There is a steep snow chute on the north side and people had cut steps into it

detail.quote: There is a steep snow chute on the north side and people had cut steps into it
detail.text: Did the pass after Rae Lakes yesterday and honestly it was terrifying. There is a steep snow chute on the north side and people had cut steps into it. I do not have an ice axe and I regretted it the whole way down. My legs were shaking. Please be careful if you are new like me.

extraction.quote_span: Axe mandatory in my opinion, saw someone self arrest for real

detail.quote: Axe mandatory in my opinion, saw someone self arrest for real
detail.text: Glen 5/31 NOBO. Full snow from Charlotte Lake side, the chute is intimidating but the steps are good. Axe mandatory in my opinion, saw someone self arrest for real. Rae Lakes basin is still mostly frozen and gorgeous. Bubbs was a serious ford, thigh high at noon.

facts.text: Snow left State Lakes (10,400 ft) 30 days earlier this year than the midpoint of two of the three earlier seasons on file (2024 and 2025).

evidence.name: State Lakes
evidence.detail: left May 1; earlier seasons: May 31 (2024), May 30 (2025); 2023: readings jump by more than snow can

facts.text: At State Lakes (10,400 ft), this year's highest snow water on or after April 1 was 4.7 in, the lowest of three of the four seasons on file (2024 to 2026).

evidence.name: State Lakes
evidence.detail: 4.7 in on April 2; earlier seasons: 25.7 in (2024), 23.3 in (2025)

facts.text: An estimate: snow left the pass itself between April 27 and June 24, carried from the melt-out dates at Upper Tyndall Creek (11,500 ft) and State Lakes (10,400 ft) to the pass elevation.

evidence.detail: melted out May 17, 426 ft below the pass; points to April 30 to June 18
